Q: Is there a way to write images to google sheets from R? A:

You can’t write a local PNG with range_write(); it only writes data frames.

A workaround is to upload the image to Drive, make it accessible, then write an IMAGE() formula:

library(googledrive)
library(googlesheets4)

img <- drive_upload("~/Image.png")
drive_share(img, role = "reader", type = "anyone")

url <- paste0("https://drive.google.com/uc?export=view&id=", img$id)

range_write(
  ss = URL,
  data = data.frame(x = paste0('=IMAGE("', url, '")')),
  range = "A1",
  col_names = FALSE
)

Note that the image must be accessible to Sheets, so private Drive files usually won’t render.

Q: Unable to fully uninstall built-in GitHub Copilot Chat extension from VS Code A:

There is a %100 FOSS community-maintained build of VS Code free from telemetry and AI features called VSCodium, which you will probably like. Just keep in mind Microsoft's proprietary extensions don't work there, but anything in Open VSX Registry (which is missing less and less from official marketplace nowadays) will (another editor which uses Open VSX is Eclipse Foundation's Theia).

Q: How to disable AI autocomplete in VS Code? A:

In version 1.104, released in September 2025, Visual Studio Code has added the setting chat.disableAIFeatures which disables all built-in AI features when set to true.

{
  "chat.disableAIFeatures": true
}

– settings.json

Also see

  • Release notes | August 2025 (version 1.104) | microsoft/vscode-docs | github.com
  • How to disable all AI features in VSCode | shonebinu.com

Q: Unable to click button from menu shown by clicking a button using Selenium A:

It seems problem is because Junior is not INSIDE button with Select age but it is in some parent-sibling element.

So it may need to find parent object

petages = driver.find_element(By.XPATH, "//section[@itemprop='offers']/header")

and after clicking Select age you have to search Junior in this object, not in button

junclick = petages.find_element(By.XPATH, '//*[text()="Junior"]').click()

you may even search button Select age in this section using first xpath

petages.find_element(By.CLASS_NAME, "_container_1dlh7_1._size__xl_1dlh7_72").click()

Full code used for tests different combinations:

It can search button with different text Junion, Newborn, Teen

from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver import Chrome
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By


def petjunior(driver, text="Junior"):
    print("petjunior ...")

    print("pettages ...")

    petages = driver.find_element(By.XPATH, "//section[@itemprop='offers']/header")

    print("petmenu ...")

    # - use last button -
    # petmenu = driver.find_elements(
    #    By.CLASS_NAME, "_container_1dlh7_1._size__xl_1dlh7_72"
    # )[-1].click()

    # - search in section -
    # petmenu = petages.find_element(
    #    By.CLASS_NAME, "_container_1dlh7_1._size__xl_1dlh7_72"
    # ).click()
    petmenu = petages.find_element(By.XPATH, '//*[@title="Select age"]').click()

    # - search directly button with text -
    # petmenu = driver.find_element(By.XPATH, '//*[@title="Select age"]').click()

    print(f"click ... {text}")

    # - search 'junior' in section, not inside button
    xpath = f'//*[text()="{text}"]'
    print(f"xpath ... {xpath}")
    junclick = petages.find_element(By.XPATH, xpath).click()
    # time.sleep(5)


def cookies(driver):

    # driver.find_element(

Q: the octal representations of bytes range from 000 to 377? A:

Standard Earth Dozenal Time 20₁₂ Dozenal Hours = 1 Day 80₁₂ Dozenal Minutes = 1 Hour 80₁₂ Dozenal Seconds = 1 Minute 0:00:00₁₂ to 1B:7B:7B₁₂ Hours: 0₁₂ to 1B₁₂ Minutes: 00₁₂ to 7B₁₂ Seconds: 00₁₂ to 7B₁₂ 10:00₁₂ AM / PM

Q: Why did GCC drop the progbits flag in .section directives for objects in .data, .rodata? A:

Looks like just a simplification of the asm output to remove redundant attributes which must have already been the default.

@progbits is the default (in GAS, the GNU assembler) for at least some standard section names like .data, .rodata, and .text. I guess this also applies to any section that's .data.* or .rodata.*. In hand-written asm with GAS you definitely don't need to specify @progbits for standard section names like .text. Again, from the fact that the GCC output omits @progbits, we can infer that it must be the default at least for those .text.* and similar sections.

Or maybe @progbits is the default in general? So you have to specify @nobits on any section you don't want to be emitted into the output, except for .bss which is automatically @nobits.

I checked the GAS manual (both the .section entry and the chapter on Sections); I didn't see a mention of @progbits or @nobits being a default. (The sections chapter documents that .bss doesn't take space in the object file / executable, though. So it is @nobits, but it doesn't use that attribute in the description).

Q: How do I start building a custom AOSP-based OS for a POS device? A:

Usually, POS terminals implement a separate system privileged application that is installed as Device Owner and has the necessary policies with restrictions, or, as an option, manufacturer create their own Launcher for this purpose.

To implement what you want, changes at the bootloader level are not needed.

Most of what you need can be implemented using Android Enterprise capabilities. This is sample app from Google: https://github.com/googlesamples/android-testdpc
